De Deo colendo." and the chapter text to the foot. No marginal notes on this page. The strip at the left edge shows fragments of the facing page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Et sic utraq; causa prima & secunda ratione modi agendi est particularis, quia utraque hoc modo agit, ut ambæ omnem gradum entitatis in actione & effecto, concurrendo, attingant: Ratione vero obiecti potest causa prima dici universalis, quia ad omnia obiecta, effecta, actiones; Secunda particularis, quia ad certa obiecta, effecta, actiones, operando concurrit, & ex hac proin discriminatio & denominatio desumenda.
Atque hæc de concursu divino, materia valde utili, ardua præsertim ac sublimi, paulo fusius adduxisse visum fuit.
main_text.head: CAP. XXIII. De Deo colendo.
main_text.p: HActenus de Deo cognoscendo satis fusè egimus, sequitur ut de eodem colendo paucis agamus.

I. Deum esse summè & perfectissimè colendum, ex præcedentibus liquido liquidiùs liquet. Ex eo quòd Deus sit Ens non [illegible, ~5 letters] omnes essentiæ divinæ proprietates ut optimè demonstrantur, ità exinde omnes omnino cultus divini partes, modos & gradus ob ocu-los

page.notes: The initial H of "HActenus" is a large woodcut-style letter joined to the word. The word after "Ens non" is set in italic and overprinted or smudged; I could not read it, so it is marked illegible. The word "ocu-" is broken at the line end and completed as "los" on the last line; I joined it as "ocu-los" and did not treat it as a catchword. The left edge strip holds the neighbouring page's text and is excluded. The ornament rule between the two paragraphs and the chapter heading are not text.
